label: Aristotle, Physics VII.1, 241b24-242a15… supports Whatever is being moved in a respect is…
note: Physics VII.1, 241b24 (Ἅπαν τὸ κινούμενον ὑπό τινος ἀνάγκη κινεῖσθαι): everything that is in motion must be moved by something, the thesis the prima via restates as omne quod movetur ab alio movetur. It bears on the premise for physical change only (DISAMB-MOTION), and Aristotle's mover may be a part of the same divisible whole, which the premise also allows (the mover y is not required to differ from x). Aristotle states no respect index; the premise's 'in that respect' is Aquinas's addition. The bound Lean reading (EveryMovingThingMovedBySomethingReading) is an opaque Prop, so no formal step connects them.
